name: Cornbread-Topped Turkey Casserole
ingredients: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 2.2 cans (651 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 6.5 oz (186 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stir the condensed cream of mushroom soup together with the onion powder, poultry seasoning, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold in the diced turkey breast, the frozen peas, and the shredded cheddar. The filling should be thick, since the cornbread pulls moisture out of it as it bakes.
Spread the filling into a greased 9x13 pan and press it into an even layer all the way to the corners.
Whisk the corn muffin mix with the milk and eggs just until combined. Lumps are fine; overmixed cornbread bakes tough.
Pour the batter over the filling and spread it gently to the edges with the back of a spoon so it seals the pan.
Bake at 400F for 30 to 35 minutes, until the cornbread is golden and a toothpick pushed into the topping comes out clean.
Rest 15 minutes before portioning. Cornbread finishes setting as it cools and will crumble if you cut it hot.

name: Cottage Pie
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water until a knife slides through with no resistance.
While they cook, brown the ground beef in the olive oil in a wide pot over medium high heat, breaking it up as it goes, until no pink remains.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, celery, and garlic and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then pour in the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce with the thyme and bay leaves.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the filling is thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon through it. Pull the bay leaves.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the milk and butter, season them well, and spread them over the filling in a large baking dish or two sheet pans.
Scatter the parmesan on top and bake at 400F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is browned and the edges bubble.

name: Country Pork Meatballs with Onion Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F and line two sheet pans. Put a pot of salted water on for the potatoes.

In a big bowl combine the ground pork, bread crumbs, eggs, green onions, garlic, italian seasoning, onion powder, paprika, dried thyme, salt and black pepper. Mix with your hands only until it comes together, because overworking it makes the meatballs tough.
Roll even meatballs, space them out on the sheet pans, and bake until browned and cooked through.
Peel and chunk the potatoes, boil until a fork slides in easy, then drain and mash with a little of the butter, salt and pepper.
Melt the rest of the butter in a wide pot and cook the sliced yellow onion low and slow until it turns deep golden and sweet. That patience is the whole flavor of the gravy.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for a minute, then pour in the beef broth along with the worcestershire and soy sauce. Whisk until it thickens into a glossy gravy.
Slide the baked meatballs into the gravy and let them simmer a few minutes so they drink some of it up.

name: Country-Fried Pork Chops with Bacon Gravy
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.5 lb (280 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Start the potatoes: peel, chunk, and boil them in salted water 15 to 20 minutes until fork tender. Drain, mash with the milk and a pinch of salt, and cover.
Set up the dredge: whisk the eggs in one dish and mix the flour with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper in another.
Dip each pork chop in egg, then press into the seasoned flour on both sides. Save the leftover flour for the gravy.
Chop the bacon and cook it in your big skillet until crisp. Lift the bacon out and leave the fat.
Add olive oil to the bacon fat and fry the chops in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and the centers read 145 F. Rest them on a rack.

Make the gravy: whisk about a quarter cup of the reserved seasoned flour into the drippings and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the chicken broth and simmer until thickened, then stir the bacon back in.
Portion mashed potatoes into 14 containers, top each with a chop, and ladle the bacon gravy over.

name: Cowboy Pork and Beans Biscuit Bake
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1.5 lb (635 g)
Baked Beans (generic with pork (USDA)): 78.5 oz (2223 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in a large oven-safe skillet or a wide pot until crisp, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Brown the ground pork in that bacon fat over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it goes, until it is cooked through and starting to catch color.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft, then stir in the minced garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the canned baked beans with their sauce, return the bacon, and season with salt and black pepper. Simmer five minutes so everything comes together.
Spread the mixture in a large baking dish and separate the biscuit dough into pieces, laying them across the top with a little space between so they can spread.
Bake at 375F for 25 to 30 minutes until the biscuits are golden through the middle and the beans bubble at the edges.

name: Creamy Cajun Chicken Penne Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1588 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 7 oz (198 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stir together the Cajun blend: smoked paprika, oregano, thyme, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, black pepper, and salt.
Cube the chicken breast, toss it with half the spice blend, and sear it in the olive oil and butter in your big pot until browned and cooked to 165 F. Set aside.
Saute the diced onion in the same pot until soft, about 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.

Add the penne, diced tomatoes with their juice, chicken broth, and the rest of the spice blend. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Cut the cream cheese into chunks and stir it in off the heat until fully melted and creamy.
Return the chicken and fold in most of the green onions.
Portion into 14 containers and top with the remaining green onions.

name: Creamy Chicken and Gnocchi Skillet
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 4.25 lb (1984 g)
Potato Gnocchi (Great Value): 56 oz dry (1588 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the chicken thighs and toss with the Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Sear the chicken in the vegetable oil in your big pot in batches until browned and cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
Add the butter to the pot and saute the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the gnocchi and the chicken broth. Cover and simmer 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the gnocchi are tender and most of the broth is absorbed.
Stir in the heavy cream and the thawed, squeezed-dry spinach and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce coats the gnocchi.
Return the chicken, stir in the parmesan, and taste for salt.
Portion into 14 containers while warm.

name: Creamy Ground Turkey and Chorizo Pasta
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 49.5 oz dry (1400 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 14.75 oz (420 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the pasta shells 1 minute short of package time. Before draining, scoop out and save about 3 cups of the starchy pasta water.

Brown the chorizo in a splash of oil in your big pot, breaking it up, then add the ground turkey and cook until no pink remains, seasoning with the Italian seasoning, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Add the diced zucchini and cook 4 to 5 minutes until just tender.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook 3 to 4 minutes until they blister and start to break down.
Drop the cream cheese in chunks and stir with a ladle of the reserved pasta water until it melts into a smooth sauce. Add more pasta water until it is silky.
Fold in the drained shells, lemon juice, parmesan, and basil, tossing until every shell is coated.
Portion into 14 containers while the sauce is still loose; it thickens as it cools.

name: Creamy Ground Turkey Shell Pasta
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 28 oz dry (794 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the pasta shells 1 minute short of package time, drain, and set aside.
Brown the ground turkey in half the olive oil in your big pot, breaking it up until no pink remains. Season with salt, pepper, and the Italian seasoning. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and saute the sliced mushrooms, diced onion, and diced bell pepper until the mushrooms release their water and brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir 1 to 2 minutes to cook it out.
Slowly whisk in the beef broth, then the heavy cream. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Return the turkey, stir in the parmesan, and fold in the shells until coated.
Portion into 14 containers while the sauce is still loose.

name: Creamy Ground Turkey Tortellini Skillet
ingredients: Cheese Tortellini (Great Value): 71.5 oz dry (2026 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in your big pot, breaking it up until no pink remains. Season with salt, pepper, and half the Italian seasoning.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens a shade.
Add the tomato sauce, chicken broth, and remaining Italian seasoning. Bring to a simmer.
Add the tortellini and simmer 4 to 6 minutes, stirring gently, until they are tender and puffed.
Stir in the heavy cream and the thawed, squeezed-dry spinach and simmer 2 minutes more.
Turn off the heat and stir in most of the parmesan until melted.
Portion into 14 containers and dust with the remaining parmesan.

name: Creamy Kielbasa and Potato Soup
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 10.25 oz (289 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins, dice the onion, carrots, celery and potatoes, and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and brown the sausage coins until the edges get dark. Take them out and leave the fat behind, because that fat is flavor.
Melt the butter in the same pot and cook the onion, carrots and celery until they soften, then add the garlic for a minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for a couple of minutes so it cooks out instead of tasting like paste.
Pour in the beef broth slowly while whisking, then add the diced potatoes, paprika, italian seasoning, salt and black pepper.
Simmer until the potatoes are soft enough to mash against the side of the pot, then stir in the corn.
Return the sausage, turn the heat low, and stir in the heavy cream. Warm it through without letting it boil so it stays smooth.

name: Creamy Mushroom Pork Chops over Mashed Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Start the potatoes: peel, chunk, and boil in salted water 15 to 20 minutes until fork tender. Drain and mash with a spoonful of the butter and a pinch of salt. Cover and keep warm.

Season the chops with salt and pepper and dust lightly with some of the flour. Sear in olive oil in your big skillet, 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and the centers read 145 F. Rest on a plate.
Melt the butter in the same skillet and cook the sliced mushrooms without crowding until browned, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the remaining flour and stir 1 to 2 minutes.
Whisk in the chicken broth and Worcestershire, scraping up the browned bits, then stir in the heavy cream. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
Return the chops and any juices to the gravy for a minute to warm through.
Portion mashed potatoes into 14 containers, top with a chop, and ladle mushroom gravy over each.

name: Creamy Pork Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into bite sized cubes, pat them dry, and toss them with the flour, salt and black pepper until every piece is dusted.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches. Crowding the pan steams the meat instead of searing it, so give it room and take your time.
Pull the pork out and drop the butter in, then cook the diced onion, carrots and celery until they soften and pick up the browned bits.
Add the garlic, dried thyme and italian seasoning and stir until you can smell them, about one minute.
Pour in the chicken broth along with the Worcestershire, dijon mustard, hot sauce and bay leaves, scraping the bottom of the pot clean.
Return the pork, add the cubed potatoes, and simmer covered until the meat is tender and the potatoes give way to a fork.
Fish out the bay leaves, turn the heat low, and stir in the heavy cream. Let it warm through without boiling so it stays smooth.

name: Creamy Pork Tenderloin Tagliatelle (alla Castellana)
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.75 lb (347 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the fettuccine 1 minute short of package time, drain, and toss with a little of the butter so it does not stick.
Chop the bacon and cook it in your big pot until the fat renders and it starts to crisp.

Slice the pork tenderloin into thin strips, season with salt and pepper, and add it to the bacon. Cook 4 to 5 minutes until the pork is cooked through with no pink; thin strips pass 145 F almost immediately.
Add the rest of the butter, the sliced mushrooms, and the diced onion. Cook 8 minutes or so until the mushrooms brown, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the splash of chicken broth to deglaze, then the heavy cream. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Fold in the fettuccine and toss until every ribbon is coated. Season generously with black pepper.
Portion into 14 containers while the sauce is still loose.

name: Creamy Tomato Ground Turkey Gnocchi
ingredients: Potato Gnocchi (Great Value): 61.75 oz dry (1750 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 18.5 oz (525 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in your big pot, breaking it up until no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, Italian seasoning, and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in the tomato sauce and chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Add the gnocchi and simmer 5 to 6 minutes, stirring so they do not stick, until tender.
Stir in the heavy cream and parmesan and simmer 2 minutes more until the sauce is creamy and coral colored.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover, and let it melt 2 to 3 minutes off the heat (or broil briefly if your pot is oven safe).
Portion into 14 containers, giving each its share of the melted cheese top.

name: Creamy Turkey Gnocchi Soup
ingredients: Potato Gnocchi (Great Value): 58.75 oz dry (1667 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, celery and carrots small and sweat them in the olive oil in your big pot over medium heat until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic, the dried thyme and the Italian seasoning and stir for a minute until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring it to a simmer, and let the vegetables get fully tender.
Add the gnocchi and cook until they float and turn soft, only a few minutes. Do not walk away here.
Stir in the cooked turkey breast, the thawed chopped spinach, the heavy cream and the milk, then bring it back to a bare simmer without letting it boil.
Season with salt and black pepper and let it sit off the heat for a few minutes so it thickens up.

name: Creamy Turkey and Rice Soup with Mushrooms
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.5 lb (265 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the wild rice separately per the package until tender and set it aside. It takes longer than white rice, so start it first.
Chop the bacon and render it in your big pot with the olive oil until crisp, then lift the bacon out and leave the fat behind.
Add the butter, then the diced onion, celery and carrots, and cook until soft. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they give up their water and start to brown.
Stir in the garlic, the dried thyme and the Italian seasoning, then sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for two minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Pour in the chicken broth slowly while stirring so the roux does not lump, then simmer until it thickens.
Add the cooked wild rice, the turkey breast and the heavy cream, warm it through without boiling, then finish with the lemon juice, the reserved bacon, salt and black pepper.

name: Crockpot Mexican Turkey Casserole
ingredients: Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 5 cans (1387 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2.5 cans (625 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 1 can (404 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 9.75 oz (277 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and brown the ground turkey hard, breaking it into crumbles. This is the only stovetop step and it is worth every minute.
Add the diced onion to the turkey and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the chili powder, ground cumin, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper and cook one minute more.
Scrape the turkey mixture into the slow cooker and add the dry rice, the enchilada sauce, the drained black beans, the diced tomatoes with their juice, and the drained corn.
Stir in the diced red and green bell peppers and mix everything thoroughly so the rice is fully submerged. Rice sitting above the liquid line will stay hard.
Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 3, until the rice is tender and has absorbed nearly all the liquid.
Resist lifting the lid while it cooks. Every peek costs you fifteen to twenty minutes of cooking time in a slow cooker.
Scatter the Mexican cheese blend over the top, replace the lid, and let it melt for 10 minutes off the heat before portioning.

name: Curried Sausages with Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep skillet and brown the sausages whole on all sides. Take them out and set them aside once they have color.
Slice the onions, slice the carrots into coins and mince the garlic.
Cook the onions in the sausage drippings until soft, then add the garlic and the carrots.
Sprinkle the flour and the curry powder over the vegetables and stir for a full minute. Cooking the curry powder in the fat is what wakes it up, and skipping this leaves it tasting dusty.
Stream in the chicken broth while stirring so no lumps form, add the sugar, and bring the gravy to a simmer until it thickens.
Slice the browned sausages into thick coins, return them to the pan, and simmer so they soak up the gravy and finish cooking through.
Stir in the frozen peas at the very end, season with salt and black pepper, and serve it over hot rice.

name: Curry Ground Turkey Bowls
steps: Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft, then stir in the chili powder and cumin.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and coconut milk and stir it all together.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and turns rich.
Serve the curry over cooked white rice.

name: Dak Galbi (Korean Chicken and Cabbage Skillet)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2333 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 4.75 tbsp (25 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice cakes in warm water for 20 minutes if they came refrigerated or frozen, so they soften evenly instead of staying hard in the center.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, red pepper flakes, and black pepper with the chicken broth into a marinade.
Cut the chicken breast into bite sized pieces and toss with about half the marinade. Let it sit 20 minutes.

Cut the cabbage into wide ribbons, the sweet potato and carrot into thin slices, and the onion into wedges. Thin slices matter for the sweet potato, because it cooks slower than everything else in the pan.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet over high heat and cook the chicken until it browns at the edges, working in batches so the pan stays hot.
Add the sweet potato, carrot, onion, and drained rice cakes with the rest of the marinade and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the rice cakes soften.
Fold in the cabbage last and cook 5 more minutes, just until it wilts but still has bite. Overcooked cabbage turns watery and takes the sauce with it.

name: Dutch Oven Pork Loin Roast with Potatoes and Gravy
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the pork loin dry, season it hard with salt, black pepper, dried thyme and Italian seasoning, and sear it on every side in olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven until deeply browned.
Lift the roast out. Cook the chopped onion, carrots and celery in the same pot until they start to color, then stir in the minced garlic and the bay leaves.
Pour in the apple juice, scrape every browned bit off the bottom, then add the chicken broth.
Set the roast back on the vegetables, tuck the quartered potatoes around it, cover, and roast at 325F for about 90 minutes until the pork is tender.
Move the roast and the vegetables to a board and let the meat rest 15 minutes before you slice or shred it.
Set the pot over medium heat, whisk the flour into the butter to make a paste, stir it into the drippings, and simmer until the gravy thickens. Season and pull the bay leaves.

name: Ecuadorian Hornado (Slow Roasted Pork) Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mash the peeled garlic with salt into a paste, then blend it with the achiote paste, the lime juice, ground cumin and black pepper into a thick marinade.
Score the fat cap on the pork shoulder in a crosshatch and rub the marinade into every cut and across the whole roast. Cover and refrigerate overnight if you can.
Set the pork in a roasting pan, pour the beef broth into the bottom, dot the top with the butter, and cover tightly with foil.
Roast at 300F for about 4 hours, basting with the pan juices once an hour, until the meat pulls away from the bone.
Uncover, raise the oven to 425F, and roast 25 to 30 minutes more until the outside is deeply browned and crisp.
Boil the potatoes until tender while the roast rests, then pull the pork apart and spoon the skimmed pan juices over everything.

name: Ecuadorian Seco de Pollo
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3572 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the chicken thighs with the ground cumin, dried oregano, salt and black pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high and brown them in batches until deeply colored, then set them aside.
Stir the achiote paste into the hot oil and let it bloom for 30 seconds. The oil will turn bright orange, and that color is what ends up in every bite.
Add the diced onion, diced green bell pepper and garlic and cook 6 to 8 minutes until soft and the onions are translucent.
Blend about half the cilantro with the orange juice into a green puree and pour it in, along with the diced tomatoes and the beef broth. Scrape the bottom of the pot clean.
Return the chicken and all its juices, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook at a low bubble for 60 to 75 minutes until the chicken is falling apart and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
While it braises, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Break the chicken into big shreds in the sauce, stir in the rest of the chopped cilantro off the heat, and fold the cooked rice through.

name: Escondidinho de Carne (Brazilian Beef and Potato Bake)
ingredients: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 17.25 oz (487 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 11 oz (314 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and boil the potatoes until they fall apart on a fork, then drain them well and let the steam escape for a minute.
Mash the potatoes with the milk, butter, parmesan cheese, salt, and black pepper until smooth, then set the mash aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and cook the diced yellow onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground beef, break it up, and cook until browned with no pink remaining, then drain off the excess fat.
Stir in the chili powder, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper, then take the pan off the heat and fold in the cream cheese and the chopped cilantro until melted through.
Spread the beef in an even layer in a large baking dish and blanket it with the mashed potato.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top and bake at 400 degrees until melted, bubbling, and browned in spots.

name: Ethiopian Doro Wat Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks and toss with the lemon juice and a big pinch of salt. Let them sit while you cook the onions.

Finely chop the red onions and cook them dry in your big pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, 15 to 20 minutes until soft and deeply golden. This slow onion melt is the backbone of doro wat, so do not rush it.
Add the vegetable oil, garlic, and ginger and cook 2 minutes. Stir in the berbere and paprika and toast 1 to 2 minutes until brick red and fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the chicken broth. Simmer 10 minutes to marry the sauce.
Add the chicken and simmer gently, partially covered, 25 to 30 minutes until it reaches 165 F and the sauce has thickened. Stir in the butter at the end for gloss.
Meanwhile, hard boil the eggs: 11 minutes in boiling water, then an ice bath, then peel. Prick or slash each egg lightly and let them warm in the sauce for the last 5 minutes.
Portion into 14 containers with a hard boiled egg or so in each, covered in sauce.

name: Ethiopian Berbere Ground Beef (Minchet Abish)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the yellow onions fine and cook them in a dry pot over medium-low heat until they release their water and start to collapse.
Add the butter and keep cooking the onions slowly until they are soft, golden, and jammy. This is the step that makes the dish, so do not hurry it.
Stir in the garlic and the berbere seasoning and cook for a minute so the spices bloom in the butter.
Add the ground beef, break it up thoroughly, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and enough water to loosen it, then simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste and let it sit off the heat for a few minutes to settle.
Cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath.

name: Farmhouse Pork Chop and Stuffing Casserole
ingredients: Cream of Chicken Soup (generic condensed (USDA)): 3.5 cans (1043 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the sandwich bread and dry the cubes on a sheet pan at 300F for about 20 minutes so they can soak up liquid without turning to mush.
Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the diced celery and onion until soft and translucent, then pour the whole buttery mix over the bread cubes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and the chicken broth, season with salt and black pepper, and pour it over the bread. Toss until every cube is damp but not soaked.
Spread the stuffing in a large greased baking dish and press it flat.
Season the pork chops with salt and black pepper, sear them in a hot skillet for color, and nest them into the stuffing.
Spoon the cream of chicken soup over the chops, cover with foil, and bake at 350F for 45 minutes, then uncover for 15 more to brown the top.

name: Fasolka po Bretonsku (Polish Baked Beans with Kielbasa)
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1 lb (467 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon, slice the smoked sausage into coins, dice the onion and mince the garlic. Drain and rinse the beans.
Render the bacon in a heavy pot until the fat runs and the pieces crisp at the edges.
Add the vegetable oil and brown the sausage coins in the bacon fat until they take on color.
Cook the diced onion until soft, then add the garlic and the tomato paste and stir for a couple of minutes so the paste darkens and loses its raw edge.
Stir in the smoked paprika, regular paprika, dried thyme, oregano and bay leaves, then pour in the diced tomatoes and the beef broth.
Add the drained beans and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and coats the beans instead of pooling around them.
Pull out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately to serve underneath.

name: Filipino Beef Caldereta
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 5.5 oz (159 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into big chunks and fry them in the vegetable oil until browned on the outside, then set them aside. This keeps them from disintegrating during the braise.
Season the cubed beef with salt and pepper and brown it hard in the same pot in batches.
Cook the onion and garlic until soft, then add the tomato sauce, tomato paste, soy sauce, and the broths and scrape the bottom of the pot clean.
Return the beef, bring it to a simmer, cover, and cook low for about 2 hours until it is fork tender.
Blend the chicken livers with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth and stir the mixture back into the pot along with the peanut butter. Let it simmer 10 minutes to thicken.
Add the fried potatoes and carrots, the sliced red and green peppers, and the olives and cook another 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Stir the shredded cheddar in off the heat until it melts into the sauce, then taste for salt.

name: Filipino Beef Pares Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes. Sear them hard in a little oil, in batches, until they have real color on at least two sides.
Add chopped onion, half the garlic, and the ginger to the pot and cook until the onion goes soft and translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Add bay leaves and black pepper, scraping the browned bits off the bottom.
Cover and simmer low for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the beef pulls apart with a spoon. Add water if the pot gets too dry.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes and let the sauce reduce until it coats the beef instead of pooling around it.
For the garlic rice, fry the remaining sliced garlic in the rest of the oil until golden, then toss in the cooked cold rice and stir until every grain is coated and hot.
Finish with sliced green onions over the beef.

name: Filipino Chicken Afritada Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.5 lb (3360 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks and pat dry. Brown them in batches in some of the vegetable oil in your big pot. Set aside.
Fry the diced potatoes and carrots in the remaining oil 5 minutes until they pick up color. Set aside with the chicken.
Saute the diced onion until soft, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes and fish sauce, bring to a simmer, and cook 10 minutes to concentrate.
Return the chicken, potatoes, and carrots. Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken reads 165 F and the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the sliced green and red bell peppers and the peas for the last 5 minutes so they keep some snap. Season with black pepper and salt to taste.
Portion into 14 containers, distributing chicken and vegetables evenly.

name: Filipino Chicken Inasal Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Make the marinade: whisk the white vinegar, lime juice, lemongrass paste, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces, toss with the marinade, and refrigerate at least 1 hour, up to overnight.
Cook the rice: 3.75 cups dry rice in a rice cooker or covered pot.
Make the annatto butter: melt the butter with the achiote paste over low heat, mashing until the butter turns deep orange.
Grill or sear the chicken over high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per side, basting generously with the annatto butter, until charred at the edges and cooked through to 165 F.
Brush the cooked chicken with any remaining baste (bring leftover baste to a brief boil first if it touched raw chicken).
Portion rice into 14 containers and top with the basted chicken.

name: Filipino Pork Giniling (Filipino Picadillo)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Hard boil the 12 eggs: cover with cold water, bring to a boil, kill the heat, lid on for 12 minutes, then cool, peel, and slice.
Heat the vegetable oil in your biggest pot and cook the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add the ground pork and break it up as it browns. Cook until no pink remains, then stir in the soy sauce and fish sauce.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and tomato paste. Add the diced potatoes, carrots, and red bell pepper, cover, and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are fork tender.
Stir in the frozen peas and golden raisins and simmer 5 more minutes. Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Portion into 14 containers and divide the sliced eggs across the tops.

name: Filipino Pork Menudo Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into cubes and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot, stir in the achiote paste until it colors the oil, then brown the pork in batches.
Add the diced yellow onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and fish sauce, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until the pork is starting to turn tender.
Add the cubed potatoes, carrots, and chicken livers and simmer uncovered until the vegetables are cooked through and the sauce reduces.
Fold in the chickpeas, diced green and red bell peppers, and golden raisins, and cook just until the peppers soften but keep some bite.
Taste and adjust the salt, then cook rice separately to serve underneath.

name: Five Spice Turkey Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 45.5 oz dry (1293 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the mushrooms thick. Thin slices vanish into a broth like this, and you want them to stay recognizable in the bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes without stirring much, so they release their water and then start to brown instead of steam.
Add the minced garlic and the five spice powder and stir for one minute. This blooming step wakes the spice up, and it is the whole reason this bowl tastes like more than salty broth.
Pour in the chicken broth, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer 15 minutes so the flavors marry.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat and taste. It should read savory first and sweet second.
Boil the lo mein noodles just short of done, drain them, rinse them cold so they stop cooking, and move them into your weighed pot.

name: Slow Cooker French Onion Pot Roast Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice all the onions thin. This is the long part of the prep, so put on something to listen to and get through it.
Season the chuck roast with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and thyme, and set it in the slow cooker.
Pile the sliced onions over and around the roast. They will look like far too much and they will cook down to a fraction of that.
Pour in the beef broth and the Worcestershire sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the roast shreds under a fork and the onions have collapsed into the liquid.
Shred the beef in the cooker and stir it through the onions and broth so every strand picks up the gravy.
Cook the rice separately while the beef finishes.

name: Frito Pie Walking Taco Casserole
ingredients: Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 2.3 cans (662 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a big pot and cook the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and break it up as it browns. Cook until no pink remains, then stir in the taco seasoning and salt.
Add the drained kidney beans, the diced tomatoes with green chilies with their juice, and the tomato sauce. Simmer 10 minutes so it thickens into a proper chili.
Spread the chili into a baking dish, top with the Mexican cheese blend, and bake at 350F until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 15 minutes.
Portion the chili into 14 containers. Keep the corn chips in the bag; add a handful on top after reheating so they stay crunchy instead of turning to mush.

name: Georgian Chicken Chakhokhbili
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.75 lb (3500 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the chicken into large pieces and season it with salt and black pepper. Heat a dry heavy pot over medium-high and brown the chicken in the vegetable oil in batches until it takes color, then set it aside.

Slice all the onions thin and add them to the pot. Cook them over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until they are completely soft and starting to turn gold. This is the largest ingredient in the dish, so it deserves the time.
Add the garlic, minced jalapeno and diced red bell pepper and cook 3 more minutes.

Return the chicken with its juices, add the diced tomatoes and the bay leaves, and stir. Add no water at all; the tomatoes and onions provide everything this braise needs, and that concentration is the whole point of chakhokhbili.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened around it.
Stir in the white vinegar and taste. It should read savory first with a sharp edge behind it. Adjust the salt now, while everything is hot.
Kill the heat, pull the bay leaves, and fold in the whole pile of chopped cilantro so it wilts but stays green. Cook the rice separately and fold it in or serve the braise over it.

name: Ghanaian Shoko (Beef and Spinach Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into bite sized cubes, season with salt and pepper, and brown them hard in oil in batches. Set the beef aside.
Blend the diced tomatoes, a large share of the onion, the bell peppers, jalapeno, garlic, and ginger into a rough puree.
Cook the remaining chopped onion in the same pot until soft, then pour in the puree and fry it, stirring often, until it darkens and the raw tomato smell is gone.
Grind the peanuts to a coarse meal and stir them in along with the coriander, cumin, and other pantry spices.
Return the beef with the beef broth, cover, and simmer 60 to 90 minutes until the beef is fork tender and the sauce has tightened.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook 5 more minutes, just until it is fully wilted and folded through.
Cook the rice separately, then taste the stew and correct the salt.

name: Giouvetsi (Greek Beef and Orzo Bake)
ingredients: Orzo Pasta (Great Value): 30.75 oz dry (875 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the beef chuck roast into large cubes and season them with salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe pot and brown the beef in batches, giving each piece room, then set it aside.
Cook the diced red onions and carrots in the same pot until softened and picking up the browned bits.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook it until it darkens, then add the diced tomatoes, ground cinnamon, sugar, and beef broth.
Return the beef, cover, and braise in a moderate oven until the meat is fork tender, which is the point of no return for this dish. Do not rush it.
Stir the dry orzo into the pot with enough hot water or broth to cover it, since the pasta will drink a surprising amount.
Return it to the oven uncovered until the orzo is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed, then stir in most of the parmesan cheese and scatter the rest over the top.

name: Goan Pork Vindaloo Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Soak the dried arbol chiles in hot water until they soften, then blend them with most of the garlic, the white vinegar, the cumin, coriander, garam masala, cinnamon, turmeric, chili powder and dijon mustard into a smooth paste.

Cut the pork shoulder into large cubes and coat it in the paste. Let it marinate at least an hour, and overnight in the fridge if you have the time. This is the step that makes it taste like vindaloo instead of curry.
Slice the onions and the jalapenos.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the onions slowly until they go deep golden and sweet.
Add the marinated pork with all its paste and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the meat browns and the paste darkens and smells toasted rather than raw.
Add the diced tomatoes, the sliced jalapenos, the brown sugar, the bay leaves, salt and enough water to just cover, then bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and braise low until the pork shreds under a fork, then stir in the lime juice off the heat and cook the rice separately to serve underneath.

name: Greek Beef and Chickpea Bowls
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (200 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse it, then simmer covered with water until tender and set it aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet, add the ground beef, and break it up as it browns. Cook until no pink remains.
Season the beef with the garlic powder, dried oregano, dried dill, salt, and black pepper, and let it toast in the spices for 2 minutes.
While the beef cooks, dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and slice the red onion thin.
Build each container: rice on the bottom, seasoned beef, a scoop of hummus, a scoop of Greek yogurt, then cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and crumbled feta.
Portion evenly across 14 containers. Keep the yogurt and hummus to one side of the box if you plan to reheat, then stir them in after.

name: Greek Ground Turkey Lemon Rice Bowls
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (200 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat a splash of the olive oil in your biggest pot and cook the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground turkey and break it up as it browns. Cook until it reaches 165F and no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the rinsed rice, chicken broth, lemon juice, and enough water to cook the rice. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir in the rest of the olive oil and the sliced olives, then taste for salt. Lemon rice should make your mouth water a little.
Portion into 14 containers and top each with crumbled feta.

name: Greek Pork Souvlaki Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the olive oil, white vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, dijon mustard, dried oregano, italian seasoning, paprika, salt, and black pepper into a marinade.
Cut the pork tenderloin into large cubes, toss them in the marinade, and refrigerate for at least four hours and ideally overnight.
Heat the oven hot, around 425 degrees, and cut the red onions into thick wedges.
Spread the marinated pork and the onion wedges on sheet pans in a single layer, drizzled with the vegetable oil. Crowding the pan steams the meat instead of browning it, so use two pans.
Roast until the pork is cooked through and the edges are browned and caught in spots.
Cook the rice according to the package while the pork roasts.
Squeeze any remaining lemon juice over the hot pork straight off the pan and let it rest a few minutes before portioning.

name: Greek Stifado (Beef and Onion Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into big chunks, dry them well, and season with salt and pepper. Brown them hard in olive oil in batches, then set them aside. Do not rush this part, and do not crowd the pan.
Peel the onions and cut them into thick wedges. Add them to the pot with the rest of the oil and cook over medium heat until they soften and start to color, about 20 minutes.
Pour in the red wine vinegar and let it bubble down while you scrape every brown bit off the bottom of the pot. That fond is the backbone of the sauce.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook it for a minute, then add the diced tomatoes, beef broth, chicken broth, bay leaves, allspice, and nutmeg.
Return the beef, bring it to a bare simmer, cover, and leave it alone for about 2 hours. Stifado does not want to be stirred every five minutes. The onions need to be left in peace to collapse.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes so the sauce reduces and thickens around the meat. Pull the bay leaves out, taste for salt, and add a splash more vinegar if it needs brightening.

name: Greek Turkey Fasolakia Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a wide heavy pot and cook the sliced onion over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until it is soft and sweet, then add the garlic for one minute.
Add the ground turkey and brown it, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, the oregano, cumin, bay leaves, salt, and black pepper, and let it bubble for 5 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into chunks and add them along with the green beans and enough water to come about halfway up the vegetables.
Cover and simmer on low for 35 to 40 minutes, until the potatoes are fork tender and the beans have gone soft and olive-drab. Do not chase bright green beans here, that is a different dish.
Pull the bay leaves, stir in the lemon juice, and taste for salt. Let it sit off the heat for 10 minutes so it tightens up.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the braise in its own pot for portioning.

name: Greek Turkey Giouvetsi (Baked Orzo)
ingredients: Orzo Pasta (Great Value): 27.75 oz dry (784 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the turkey breast into chunks and season with salt and pepper. Brown it in the olive oil in a wide oven-safe pot, in batches, then set it aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot until soft, about 8 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, nutmeg, a pinch of sugar, and black pepper for one minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, the tomato sauce, and the beef broth, return the turkey, and bring it to a simmer.
Cover and bake at 350F for 45 minutes, until the turkey is tender and cooked through to 165F and the sauce has reduced.

Stir in the dry orzo along with enough hot water to keep everything loose, since orzo drinks more liquid than you expect. Cover and bake 20 minutes more, stirring once halfway so it does not stick to the bottom.
Uncover, scatter the parmesan over the top, and bake 5 minutes to melt it in.
Let it rest 10 minutes, then move it into your weighed pot and fold gently so the orzo and the turkey are evenly mixed.

name: Greek Turkey Meatballs with Lemon Orzo
ingredients: Orzo Pasta (Great Value): 28 oz dry (794 g)
Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (196 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F. In a big bowl, mix the ground turkey, eggs, bread crumbs, grated red onion, garlic, chopped mint, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper until just combined.
Roll the mix into meatballs, about 3 per serving, and set them on lined sheet pans. Slice the bell peppers into strips and spread them on the pans around the meatballs with a little of the olive oil.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes until the meatballs hit 165F in the center and the peppers have softened.
Meanwhile, boil the orzo until just tender, drain, and toss it with the butter and lemon juice while it is hot.
Stir the Greek yogurt with half the feta and a squeeze of lemon to make the sauce.
Portion orzo, meatballs, and peppers into 14 containers. Top with the yogurt sauce, olives, and the rest of the feta.

name: Greek Turkey Moussaka
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the eggplant into rounds, salt them, and let them sit 20 minutes to draw out water. Pat them dry, brush them with the olive oil, and roast at 425F for about 25 minutes until they are soft and browned.
While the eggplant roasts, cook the diced onion in a large pot until soft, add the garlic for a minute, then brown the ground turkey until it reaches 165F.

Add the tomato sauce, beef broth, cinnamon, oregano, red wine vinegar, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Simmer 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and almost dry, because a wet meat layer means a soggy casserole.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook two minutes, then pour in the milk slowly while whisking until it thickens. Off the heat, whisk in the beaten eggs, the parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Layer the roasted eggplant and the meat sauce in your baking pans, pour the bechamel over the top, and smooth it flat.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes until the top is set and golden, then let it rest at least 20 minutes so the squares hold together when you cut them.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and cut the moussaka into 14 even squares.
